newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Energy's Maui F, D oil to be priced off Tapis.
newsitem.headline: FCL Energy's Maui F, D oil to be priced off Tapis.

text.p: Oil from Fletcher Challenge Energy's Maui D and F Sands resource would be priced off Tapis, Asia's benchmark, FCL corporate communications manager Barry Akers said on Monday.
FCL Energy last week began shipping oil from the newly-developed F and D Sands resource in the Maui Field, off the coast of the west North Island province of Taranaki.
The shipment culminated a three-year development programme, which appraised a resource of about 22 million barrels, of which FCL Energy's share is around 15 million.
F and D are producing a total of 35,000 barrels per day.

The joint venture partners, which include Royal Dutch Shell Group and Todd Petroleum Mining Co Ltd, are using a floating production and storage fracility (FPSO) connected to the Maui B production platform, 50 km off the Taranaki coast, to process the crude.
The production life of the resource is around four and half years.
Akers said the waxy crude is characterised by a pour point in the range of 18-21 degrees Celcius and a cloud point in the range of 42-45 degrees. Asphaltene content is about 0.7 percent by weight.
FCL Energy's share of the resource is marketed by Fletcher Challenge Petroleum Marketing, which takes care of all FCL's crude production.
The Maui field was discovered in 1969 and was brought on stream in 1979 through 14 development wells drilled from a single platform in the Maui A area.
